newsitem.title: USA: Barshefsky says US exports benefit from WTO.
newsitem.headline: Barshefsky says US exports benefit from WTO.

text.p: Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said Wednesday the United States has enjoyed an increase of key exports, including agriculture, from its participation in the World Trade Organization.

"The WTO agreement only entered into force on January 1, 1995, but we are already seeing impressive growth in sectors that are critical to the U.S. economy and sectors where we fought hard to open markets," Barshefsky said in prepared testimony to the House Ways and Means trade subcommittee.
The panel was holding a hearing on the WTO and the ministerial conference to be held in Singapore in December.
Barshefsky said U.S. agricultural exports to WTO members grew by 28 percent in 1995 and continued to grow at a healthy pace in the first half of 1996.
"Countries that heretofore banned imports of U.S. products, such as rice and apples, were required to open their markets," she said.

"We're making sure the Committee on Agriculture is viewed by all WTO members as a forum where detailed scrutiny is given to each and every country's progress in adhering to commitments on domestic support, import performance under tariff rate quotas and export subsidies," Barshefsky added.
She said that in 1995 U.S. exports of paper to WTO members grew by more than 40 percent, construction equipment by nearly 30 percent, and chemicals and agricultural equipment by more than 25 percent.

U.S. trade policies and participation in the World Trade Organization could become a target of Reform Party presidential candidate Ross Perot, who chose anti-free-trade econmist Pat Choate as a running mate.
Choate has strongly criticized U.S. participation in the WTO as well as the North American Free Trade Agreement.
